description_en: The previously open eleven-bayphalcāhas been converted into residential spaces for several families. Kālamocanaghāṭa Phalcā West is almost identical to the Kālamocanaghāṭa Phalcā East (KAT2783), with the two buildings sharing many details such as size, carving styles, and building materials, making it appropriate to refer to them as twinphalcās. Kālamocana Ghāṭa (KAT2780) is located between these two impressivephalcās,and it can be assumed that thephalcāsprovided shelter for the many devotees frequenting theghāṭaslining the banks of the Bagmati.There is no inscriptive evidence regarding the construction of thephalcās;however, architectural features, such as the carving style of columns and arches, indicate that construction likely occurred between the Śāha and Rāṇā periods (e.g. mid 19th century).An inventory from 1982 CE (VS 2039) reports the dilapidated condition of thephalcāsand recommends renovation. A photograph depicts the poor state of the Kālamocanaghāṭa Phalcā West at that time (Inventory VS 2039, p.134). Despite its critical condition, the renovation was not undertaken, leading homeless families to repurpose the space as residences by closing the bays with brick walls to create rooms according to their needs. In contrast to the renovation and reconstruction efforts undertaken for numerous monuments along the banks of the Bāgamatī after the earthquake of 2015 CE (VS 2072), these twophalcāshave remained neglected. Prior to VS 2030, devotional songs and rituals were performed in thesephalcās.
brick_type: dāci apā (conical veneer brick), mā apā (regular fired brick)
monument_assessment: Heavily damaged (collapsed, demolished, major cracks and structural damages)
